{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.",
    "If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by adding 1–2% to forecast baseline.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a 1–3 day lag correction or reduce slope after peak.",
    "When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of divergence.",
    "If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign horizon; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.",
    "For 30-day forecasts, if model starts above 85 and true outcome drops below 80 within 10 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.",
    "If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often overfits short-term noise; use 7-day smoothing filter before forecasting."
  ]
}
